title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: for two morphisms of topoi α, β : X' ⇉ X, Grothendieck defines L(α,β) (written 𝒢 here) as the category of pairs (E, 𝔽_E). Here E ∈ X and 𝔽_E : α*E → β*E is either an arbitrary map or, in the 'resp.' variant, an isomorphism. The forgetful functor ω*(E,𝔽_E) = E is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi ω : X → L(α,β). There is a canonical 2-cell 𝔽 : ωβ ⇒ ωα. The claimed universal property is that g ↦ (g∘ω, g*𝔽) gives an equivalence from Homtop(L(α,β), Y) to the category of pairs (φ : X → Y, f : φβ ⇒ φα). In modern terms L(α,β) is the lax coequalizer, or coinserter, of α and β in the 2-category of topoi. In the isomorphism variant it is the pseudo-coequalizer, a descent-type topos.

This page proves that L is a topos.
- Giraud's conditions (a)-(c) are immediate. α* and β* are exact and commute with colimits, so colimits and finite limits of pairs are computed componentwise in X.
- The only real issue is a small generating family.
- In the isomorphism case, L is the category of cartesian sections of an evident fibred topos over the two-object diagram X' ⇉ X (fibres X' and X, transition functors α* and β*). One can then apply SGA4 'I 9.25' (presumably the result that cartesian sections of a fibred topos form a topos).
- In the non-invertible case he sketches a modified indexing diagram: X' with u : X' → X, f : X' → X'_1, v : X'_1 → X. The 'arguments of SGA4 I 9.21 and following' should give the result; the margin says 'à vérifier'.

A crossed-out line records the motivating special case: X' = X, β = id. Then L is the category of pairs (E, 𝔽_E : α*E → E), i.e. objects with a (Frobenius-type) semilinear endomorphism. The notation 𝔽 and the dossier (crystals, De Rham) strongly suggest α is a Frobenius, so that L(Frob, id) is a topos whose objects are F-objects or F-crystals.

The page then states 2-functoriality. A square (u_0, u_1) from (α,β : X' ⇉ X) to (λ,μ : Y' ⇉ Y), commuting up to isomorphism, induces L(u) : L(α,β) → L(λ,μ). This is completed on the next page, which goes on to base change for R^i v_* and to the acyclicity of injectives of L restricted to X. That acyclicity needs α_!, β_! exact. This is the setup for cohomology of F-objects (the global sections are {s : 𝔽(α*s) = β*s}, leading to a '1−F'-type long exact sequence).
errors: The previous page writes Homtop(L(α,β), X) where Homtop(L(α,β), Y) is meant.

The generating-family argument for the non-invertible (lax) case is only gestured at ('SGA4 I 9.21 et suivants donnent le résultat ....'), and Grothendieck himself marks it 'à vérifier'. It is correct, since lax colimits of topoi exist, but no proof is given here.
The SGA4 citation 'I 9.25' looks odd: the fibred-topos and cartesian-section results are in Exposé VI (and IV). This is probably a mis-numbering or a reference to a draft numbering; unsure.

ideas.what: Topos L(α,β) of pairs (E, α*E → β*E), with its universal property among topoi under X equipped with a 2-cell φβ ⇒ φα
ideas.modern_name: Coinserter / lax coequalizer (resp. pseudo-coequalizer) in the 2-category of Grothendieck topoi
ideas.usually_credited_to: General bicolimits of topoi: Moerdijk (late 1980s), Johnstone (Elephant); descent topoi and cartesian sections: SGA4 VI (Grothendieck–Verdier)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 VI treats cartesian sections of fibred topoi (projective limits of topoi); the lax-coequalizer form seems not to be stated there

ideas.what: Proof via Giraud's axioms, reducing to a small generating family, using cartesian sections of a fibred topos over X' ⇉ X
ideas.modern_name: Topos of cartesian sections; Giraud's theorem

ideas.what: Special case X' = X, β = id: topos of objects with a Frobenius-type map α*E → E (F-objects / F-crystals as sheaves on a topos)
ideas.modern_name: Topos (or stack) of F-modules; Frobenius-fixed-point / mapping-torus topos
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure as a topos-theoretic packaging. Related later work: Lichtenbaum's Weil-étale topos; Bhatt–Lurie / Drinfeld syntomification as a coequalizer of two maps

ideas.what: 2-functoriality of L(α,β) in the pair (α,β), with base-change maps for R^i v_*
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of lax colimits; base change

missed.claim: Grothendieck packages objects with Frobenius structure (E, α*E → E), and their isomorphism variant, as sheaves on a lax (resp. pseudo) coequalizer topos of two maps X' ⇉ X. He intends to compute their cohomology as the cohomology of that topos. This is structurally the same move as the modern syntomification Z_p^syn: a coequalizer of two maps of stacks whose quasi-coherent sheaves are F-gauges. It is also close to Weil-étale topoi built as mapping tori of Frobenius.
missed.quote: Prenons le cas où X'=X, β=id, donc 𝒢(α,β) = la catégorie des couples (E, 𝔽_E), 𝔽_E: α*(E) → E
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, topos-level antecedent (1965-69) of describing F-crystals and F-gauges as sheaves on a coequalizer object, with the resulting '1−F' long exact sequence for cohomology. It is of historical interest for the prehistory of syntomic and Weil-étale cohomology.

missed.claim: The lax (non-invertible) case of the topos property, and the base change / acyclicity statements on the next page, are left as 'à vérifier'.
missed.quote: les arguments de SGA4 I 9.21 et suivants donnent le résultat .... [marge] à vérifier
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Low: these were later settled in general by the theory of lax colimits of topoi.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction itself (coinserter / coequalizer of topoi) is standard and was later published by others. What is mildly notable is that Grothendieck explicitly builds a topos of Frobenius-structured objects as a lax coequalizer, in a crystalline context, prefiguring later coequalizer descriptions of syntomic and Weil-étale objects.
transcription_corrections: 'Dans le cas simplifié [?]' / 'Dans le cas non simplifié [?]' most likely refer to the invertible ('resp. isom') case versus the general non-invertible case. A plausible reading is 'cas iso' / 'cas non iso'.
The title reads 'Le foncteur est une équivalence de catégories', continuing the universal-property statement from the previous page.

The crossed-out phrase reads roughly 'on considère une catégorie topos fibrée I sur ...'. It is replaced by the triangle diagram X' →u X, f : X' → X'_1, v : X'_1 → X, 'associés aux changements de base u'.
